requiredScope: The fixed grammar and release scope remains in force.

From/Join.role: The scoped ordered product of a comma list of ordinary table occurrences.
From/Join.structure: The list is expanded into a left-associated CROSS tree, with each external table and optional ONLY policy retained at its own leaf.
From/Join.conditions: Between 2 and 61 complete ordinary table occurrences. SELECT and WHERE use the established signed int4 operand domains. Each emitted slot must belong to its resolved occurrence.
From/Join.meaning: The left-to-right product preserves every duplicate. An empty input removes all combinations. Descendants belong to the specified input unless it declares ONLY. WHERE is applied after the complete product.
From/Join.sql: Emit the product with CROSS JOIN and use an absolute table name and a distinct alias for each occurrence.

ResultColumn.role: An ordinal output field selected from an occurrence in a FROM list.
ResultColumn.structure: Result positions pair an explicit label with the already resolved field.
ResultColumn.conditions: Every signed int4 slot is visible within the current SELECT. A wildcard expands all visible physical fields in list order or the fields of its specified occurrence.
ResultColumn.meaning: Observe names, ordered positions, signed int4 metadata, integer values, NULL and duplicates. No row order is guaranteed.
ResultColumn.sql: Project the qualified physical field under its fixed output label.

externalInterpretation: Use the same absolute ordinary relations and inheritance definitions under the pinned PostgreSQL profile.
observations: Native result names, ordinals and field types
Typed row bags with NULL and repeated values
The same declaration in distinct aliases is observed as distinct occurrences
An empty list member and inherited rows in a later occurrence are distinguishable

finite.completeness: Check every product of the five dimension sets exactly once from the actual published tree, slot projection and filter.

exploration.requiredForms: Between 2 and 6 leaves, repeated table identities with distinct occurrence positions, both inheritance flags, an empty input, labels that need quoting, and WHERE addressing multiple inputs.

analysis: Unqualified star keeps declaration order across three occurrences, including repeated table identities.
A qualified wildcard reads only the last of three occurrences.
Explicit fields and WHERE read the specified occurrences in a self product.
ONLY on a later occurrence removes descendants only there.
An empty input leaves an empty bag with unchanged output metadata.
A position-dependent filter can read fields from both ends after a four-input product.
negative: A directly constructed result references a nonexistent occurrence.
Two source occurrences provide an ambiguous unqualified field.
The list contains a derived source outside the ordinary-table boundary.
The list contains an undeclared relation.
The list exceeds the checked occurrence budget.
faults: Read a later field from the first occurrence.
Replace a later scan's ONLY policy with an inherited scan.
Omit WHERE on the normalized product.

evidence.P01: Compare ordered external identities and each resolved field reference in the published graph.
evidence.P02: Verify joint scope and finite budgets at the completed statement boundary.
evidence.P03: Store only the resolved CROSS tree, references and result labels.
evidence.P04: Derive the product and filter from explicit leaves, slots and operators.
evidence.P05: Use the checked immutable closure of existing joins, predicates and results.
evidence.P06: Compare the rendered SQL and original FROM list using the same external fixtures.
evidence.Q01: Require typed refusals for invalid occurrences and invalid analysis inputs.
evidence.Q02: Require every finite identity, seeded case and analyzed case in both registered releases.
evidence.Q03: Compare projection and filter binding under products with multiple occurrences.
evidence.Q04: Measure typed metadata and row bags and independently detect each of the three faults.
evidence.Q05: Bind runtimes, selected controller, mutations and staged source to the exact candidate.

open: Lists containing joined, lateral or derived items and unsupported scalar types require distinct admission and evidence.
Widths above 61 remain in the required scope.
trust: Pinned database and resolved base-table declarations
The independent relational evaluator and archived execution controller
